newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Fall in S.African rand boosts investment - study.
newsitem.headline: Fall in S.African rand boosts investment - study.

text.p: Foreign direct investment in South Africa has been boosted over the last eight months by the rand's depreciation against the dollar, the Washington-based Investor Responsibility Research Center (IRCC) said on Tuesday.

It said in a statement that since February, about six foreign firms had opened offices or acquired affiliates or subdsidiaries in the country each month, compared with a net average of 4.5 each month in the preceding six month period.
The rand has depreciated by about 25 percent since the first run on the currency began on February 15.

"Several firms that recently acquired subsidiaries or affiliates in South Africa told IRCC that the rand's devalued status definitely sweetened their deals," Meg Voorhes, director of IRCC's Southern Africa Program, said.
- General Electric, which acquired Daimler Benz subsidiary AEG's assets in South Africa;
- Merck, which bought Logos Pharmaceuticals from Tiger Oats ;
- Mitsubishi's acquisition of South African distributor Mitsubishi South Africa Manufacturing; and
- Malaysian state-owned Petronas, which bought a 30 percent stake in petroleum company Engen.

"More significantly...the rand's slide has prompted several multinational firms to retool or add capacity at their existing plants in South Africa to increase exports out of the country," Voorhes said.
Voorhes noted that the converse was that the rand's slide meant foreign firms which imported goods into South Africa for sale would tend to be less competitive in the local market.

"This dynamic affects roughly 65 percent of all foreign firms doing business in South Africa. However, it may provide an additional incentive for some of the larger sales generators to open up local production."

Voorhes added that government's depreciation and tax holiday incentives which came into effect this month combined with the weaker rand boded well for continued growth in foreign direct investment in South Africa.

"In addition, trade pacts with the European Community and the rest of the Southern African Development Community should entice foreign firms to open up export-oriented production in South Africa," Voorhes said.
